tours.name: The Granite Gorge
tours.blurb: A mile under the rim the river reaches rock nearly two billion years old — and every rapid on the way is a side canyon's boulder pile.

keys.cap: Hance Rapids, at the head of the Upper Granite Gorge. Red Canyon comes in from the south rim and dumps boulders; the river piles over them. Every named rapid on this sheet sits at a side-canyon mouth — that is the whole mechanism.

Sockdolager. Powell's crew named it in August 1869 with a prizefighting word for the punch that ends the fight. Below here the walls are black Vishnu schist shot with pink Zoroaster granite, and Matthes' fifty-foot contours crowd until the ink runs solid.

Granite Rapids, where Monument Creek delivers. The Tonto Platform above it — that flat bench on both sides — is the top of the Tapeats Sandstone, and it carries the Tonto Trail clear across the block.

Crystal Rapid was a riffle until December 1966, when a storm dropped fourteen inches on the Kaibab and Crystal Creek rebuilt it overnight into one of the canyon's two worst. The 1903 sheet under you still shows the quiet version.

tours.name: The temples
tours.blurb: Dutton named them in 1882 for the gods of half the world; Matthes drew them at fifty-foot contours twenty years later.

keys.cap: Vishnu's Temple. Clarence Dutton named it in the Tertiary History of the Grand Cañon District (USGS Monograph 2, 1882) and the whole pantheon followed him in. Pull the slider back to 1886 and almost none of these names are printed yet.

Shiva Temple — a detached island of Kaibab limestone, and one of the very few temple names the 1886 reconnaissance sheet already carried. In 1937 the American Museum of Natural History climbed it expecting animals cut off from the rim by the canyon; the photographer Emery Kolb got up there first and left a Kodak film carton on the summit.

Wotans Throne and Freya Castle, the Norse corner off Cape Royal. The east half of this drape is the VISHNU sheet, edition of September 1907 — Matthes and Richard T. Evans mapped it in the same 1902–03 seasons as the west.
Brahma, Deva and Zoroaster Temples above Bright Angel Canyon. Each is capped by the same two formations as the rim behind it; the temples are what is left when the side canyons eat the plateau back.

tours.name: Powell's river, Powell's survey
tours.blurb: Two boat trips and a directorship — the 1886 sheet on the middle slider stop is signed by the man who ran the river.

keys.cap: Bright Angel Creek, named by Powell's 1869 party for clear water after the muddy Dirty Devil upstream. The creek follows the Bright Angel Fault, which is why the only rim-to-rim route in the canyon runs here.

The Little Colorado's mouth, where the sheet's east edge ends. Upstream in that gorge is Sipapuni, the Hopi place of emergence, and the salt trail that goes down to it — Hopi people have walked to this confluence for as long as there has been a Hopi people.

Point Sublime, named by Dutton and drawn by William Henry Holmes for the 1882 atlas. Slide to the 1886 reconnaissance: on forty miles of rim, Point Sublime and Shivas Temple are nearly the only names on the paper.

The Powell Memorial above Hopi Point went up in 1918, fifteen years after the date printed in this sheet's margin — and it is lettered on the map all the same. That is how you date the paper: the contours are Matthes' 1902–03, the culture kept being added for half a century.

tours.name: Bright Angel and the garden
tours.blurb: A Havasupai trail to a spring-fed garden, taken for a toll road, then taken for a park.

keys.cap: Havasupai Gardens — lettered 'Indian Garden' on the sheet beneath you. Havasu 'Baaja families farmed this spring-fed bench for generations; an 1882 executive order cut their land to 518 acres in Havasu Canyon, and the last family was forced out of the garden in 1928. The Board on Geographic Names restored the Havasupai name in 2022.

Grand Canyon village. The Santa Fe spur from Williams reached this rim in September 1901; El Tovar opened in January 1905 and Hopi House the same year, built by Hopi masons to Mary Colter's design. The Bright Angel Trail below it was Ralph Cameron's toll road until the county and the park pried it loose.

Phantom Ranch — Colter's 1922 cabins where Bright Angel Creek meets the river — and the Kaibab suspension bridge of 1928, whose main cables were carried down the South Kaibab Trail on the shoulders of a crew of forty-two Havasupai men.

Plateau Point, thirteen hundred feet above the river on the Tonto bench. Garden Creek runs off the fault behind it; the springs on this sheet are almost all Redwall water, and they are the reason any of these routes exist.

tours.name: The surveyors of 1902
tours.blurb: Plane table, mule and six thousand feet of relief — how the finest contours in the Survey's catalogue came to be drawn.

keys.cap: Bright Angel Point on the Kaibab Plateau, close to 8,000 feet. The credit line on the sheet reads: E. M. Douglas, geographer in charge; topography by François E. Matthes; triangulation by H. L. Baldwin, Jr. and J. T. Stewart; surveyed in 1902–1903. That is a small expedition, and it was.

Tiyo Point and the Hindu Amphitheater. The contour interval is fifty feet at 1:48,000 — fine enough that in the Redwall the lines merge into a solid band, which is exactly what a cliff should look like on paper.
Cheyava Falls, up Clear Creek — found by Matthes' party in 1903, and given the Hopi word for 'intermittent': it pours after a wet winter and stops in a dry one.

Roaring Springs, bursting straight out of the Redwall in Bright Angel Canyon. It is the only dependable water in the inner canyon on this sheet, and since 1970 it has supplied both rims through a pipeline hung down this gorge.
